This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Vnukovo International Airport in degrees Celsius on 3 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=UUWW

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Traders assign the highest implied probabilities to 30–31°C because model guidance shows only modest temperature recovery between rain bands, with small differences in timing or intensity of precipitation able to shift the daily peak by 1–2°C. eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for the highest temperature in Tel Aviv on August 4, 2026, centers on 32–33°C, reflecting current forecast guidance under a waning heatwave.** 

Israel is experiencing an extreme heat event driven by a strong subtropical ridge, with light winds, clear skies, and reduced sea-breeze moderation allowing elevated boundary-layer temperatures along the coastal plain. Official Israel Meteorological Service outlooks and ensemble models indicate the peak intensity occurs through August 3 before gradual moderation, placing Tel Aviv daytime maxima near 31–33°C on August 4. 

Climatological August averages for the region are 31–32°C, so the current setup represents modest positive anomalies that resolve primarily into the 32°C or 33°C bins. Coastal proximity to the Mediterranean continues to cap extremes compared with inland valleys, keeping probabilities for 34°C or higher low while rendering sub-31°C outcomes unlikely absent unexpected cloud cover or stronger onshore flow. Updated short-range model runs and official high-temperature observations in the next 48 hours will provide the final refinement ahead of market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Ongoing heat wave conditions across South Korea, driven by a strong North Pacific High pressure system, position 33–35°C as the most probable range for Busan’s daily maximum on August 4.** 

Persistent clear skies, high humidity, and warm southerly flow have produced extreme readings, including a confirmed 39°C high in Busan on August 1 under Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA) heat-wave warnings. These same synoptic patterns are expected to continue, though coastal sea breezes and a modest easing in the ridge may limit the peak slightly below the recent extreme. 

KMA short- and medium-range guidance, combined with ensemble model consensus, supports daytime maxima near or slightly above seasonal normals (typically 29–31°C in August), with limited precipitation risk keeping solar heating efficient. The market’s concentration on 34°C (37.5%), 35°C (25.0%), and 33°C (20.5%) reflects trader assessment of this narrow window between sustained heat and any minor marine moderation, while lower probabilities for 36°C+ or sub-32°C outcomes align with the low likelihood of rapid pattern shifts before the observation window closes. Updated KMA briefings and model runs over the next 48 hours will be the key catalysts for any probability adjustments.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Ongoing monsoon activity across Sindh, driven by strong Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal currents plus a westerly wave, is the primary factor positioning 33°C as the market leader for Karachi’s August 4 maximum. Official PMD guidance through August 5 highlights partly cloudy skies with isolated rain-wind or thundershowers, which increase cloud cover, humidity, and evaporative cooling to cap daytime heating near or slightly above seasonal norms of ~32°C. Recent AccuWeather model runs align with this, projecting 30–33°C highs for August 3–4 amid breezy conditions. These dynamics explain the combined ~92% implied probability for 32–34°C outcomes, while the low odds for 35°C+ reflect suppressed insolation and the historical tendency for monsoon spells to moderate peaks. Updated model runs and PMD briefings on August 3–4 will be key near-term catalysts.
